name: Hosah
overview: Hosah was a male Levite who served as one of the gatekeepers assigned to the west gate, a role of responsibility in the temple service. He was a descendant of Merari, one of the three sons of Levi, highlighting his Levitical lineage and his family's dedication to the service of the tabernacle and later the temple. His duties as a gatekeeper placed him in a position of guarding and managing access to the sacred precincts.
namesAndTitles: The name Hosah means 'refuge,' which may reflect a protective aspect fitting for a gatekeeper, although the name was not given by God. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 16:38.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hosah as a descendant of Merari, with inferred paternal lineage including Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah, indicating a well-documented genealogy within the Levitical family. These relationships underscore his place within a family entrusted with specific temple duties.
scriptureSignificance: Hosah's significance lies in his role as a gatekeeper from the Merarite clan of the Levites, entrusted with the important task of guarding one of the temple gates to the west. This responsibility was crucial for maintaining the sanctity and security of the temple, reflecting the organized and divinely appointed structure of temple service. His inclusion in the genealogical and functional records of the Levites emphasizes the faithfulness and order God established in worship and service.
